newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico publishes refinery expansion bidding rules.
newsitem.headline: Mexico publishes refinery expansion bidding rules.

text.p: Mexico published an international invitation Thursday to bid for a $1.2 billion expansion of its Cadereyta refinery in the northern state of Nuevo Leon via the government's Official Gazette.

"According to the contract, the winner of the invitation will be obliged to carry out all the works necessary to modernize and expand the refinery known as "Hector R. Lara Sosa" in Cadereyta, Nuevo Leon," the Official Gazette said.

The recently-announced and approved Cadeyreta project consists of installing new plants, expanding and/or modernizing existing plants, expanding ancillary services and the integration of infrastructure, such as terminals and ducts, to increase the supply of crude and the distribution of refined products, the government said.
Mexico's state-owned oil monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) is undertaking the expansion project through its refining arm Pemex Refining.
The winning bidder will be required to obtain all the financing to carry out the expansion project up to the end of the contract.
"Pemex Refining will not make any advance payment or payment while the work is in progress," the gazette said.

"Once the works are concluded, Pemex Refining will start to make quarterly payments to the contractor over a period of 12 years, those payments being for the quantities specified in the plans of the winning bidder, and only subject to change in specific cases laid out in the contract," it added.

Pemex said Wednesday that the payments to be made will come from the flow of resources generated by the project itself and outlined that expansion consists of the construction of 10 new plants and the modernisation of another six.

The expansion is aimed at producing cleaner fuels with lower sulphur content, reducing output of high-sulphur fuel oil, meeting growing regional demand for gasoline and diesel fuel, processing more heavy crude and stepping up the refinery's output to 270,000 bpd of crude from 235,000.
